children: said Thursday it has not made any decision regarding a potential issuance of debt securities, in response to a Bloomberg report that the company is considering a debut in China’s bond market as early as this year.
China is the main consumer of Vale's
iron ore, accounting for roughly half of the company's revenue, which makes it "natural" for the Vale to tap the country's market, CFO Marcelo Bacci told Bloomberg.
The CFO said the bond sale could happen "possibly still in 2026" and that Vale is "getting the company prepared for that."

The Chinese domestic bond market is still developing to international issuers, and the typical size for the issuances tends to be small, at $400M-$500M each, with short tenure for the bonds, Bacci said.
"Normally the companies are tapping two, three, five years. We are testing the waters to see if it’s possible to go beyond that," the CFO said.
An IPO initial public offering of Vale's
copper and nickel subsidiary is not a priority for at least the next 1-2 years, with the current focus on boosting production over the coming years, Bacci said.
Separately, South Korea's HMM said it signed a contract worth ~$3.5B with Vale to carry out the maritime transport of iron ore from 2030, with a contractual term of 25 years per vessel.

title: Vale weighs entry into China's bond market, CFO says
